title: Lambda Layer Version Compliance

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.76 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.76 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="lambda.amazonaws.com" eventName="UpdateFunctionConfiguration"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.76_lambda_layer_version_com_76"
| sort -_time
description: Outdated layers carry vulnerable dependencies; enforcing approved layer ARNs avoids shadow IT libraries in functions.
value: Detecting lambda layer version compliance early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Maintain CSV lookup of approved layer version ARNs. Alert on attach of unapproved layer or version drift weekly scan via `ListFunctions`. Integrate with CI/CD to block deploys pre-merge.
visualization: Table (function, layer, user), Bar chart (non-compliant functions), Timeline (changes).

dataModelAcceleration: Change (All_Changes): for CloudTrail management events mapped to CIM. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: CI/CD and hotfix deploys that swap Lambda layers; compare layer ARNs to the service owner before flagging as drift.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Maintain CSV lookup of approved layer version ARNs. Alert on attach of unapproved layer or version drift weekly scan via `ListFunctions`. Integrate with CI/CD to block deploys pre-merge.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="lambda.amazonaws.com" eventName="UpdateFunctionConfiguration"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.76_lambda_layer_version_com_76"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect lambda layer version compliance. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_76_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (function, layer, user), Bar chart (non-compliant functions), Timeline (changes)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of lambda layer version compliance so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
